analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: a new changelog entry (changelog.d/provider-app-attest-worker.md), docs/architecture/components/provider.md and docs/architecture/security/attestation.md. No source or executable code is visible in this batch, so the implementation behind these claims is not reviewed.

Security-relevant claims documented:
- A default-off App Attest worker candidate runs as another invocation of the same signed executable. The inference X25519 key stays in the parent only and is never exported to the worker or persisted (provider.md invariant 2, head lines 130-133). This is consistent with A-003 and T-011.
- Apple-exchange replies use AppAttestShadowReply, a capability bound to the originating NWConnection. The transport is rechecked immediately before submission, so late native callbacks cannot send an old proof over a replacement connection (attestation.md head patch; provider.md head lines 104-109). This tightens the previous wording, which only covered the case after the reader had consumed the disconnect. It relates to T-053.
- Worker retirement is chained before the next transport starts verification. Update install and restart are fenced on confirmed worker retirement. A failed reap withholds drain completion or postpones the update. A fresh prepare may retry retained-owner cleanup only after a failed update returns to idle, never after terminal shutdown. No worker-stall recovery restarts inference or falls back to in-process Apple work.
- The protocol-1 endpoint-resumption responder is installed without the worker flag. It does no Apple operation, makes no model-state change and persists no key. It proves custody only, and platform authorization remains authoritative.
- The changelog states that background `darkbloom start` preserves the exact worker opt-in and keeps native diagnostic and fault flags out of the daemon. This touches the passthroughEnvKeys allowlist (provider.md invariant 4) and should be checked in code.

Nothing here changes the coordinator trust model or the TB-011 and TB-002 boundaries. The qualification caveats are stated honestly in the docs.

Open items for a code-level pass:
- Verify the worker child cannot obtain the X25519 key through inherited file descriptors, environment or arguments.
- Verify the worker IPC authenticates the parent and that the worker cannot be spoofed.
- Verify the daemon env and flag allowlist behavior.
- Verify the reply capability's connection check is atomic with the write.
